newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait crown prince in good condition - family.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait crown prince in good condition - family.

text.p: Kuwaiti Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah is in good condition after fainting on Tuesday, a senior ruling family member said on Wednesday.
Sheikh Saad fell and suffered "slight bruises," a senior member of the al-Sabah ruling family told Reuters. "Thank God His Highness is in a good condition."

On the midnight (2100 GMT Tuesday) news state-run Kuwait television showed Sheikh Saad receiving officials from fellow Gulf Arab states Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday before he was taken to hospital.
The official Kuwaiti news agency and radio issued an official statement saying Sheikh Saad's condition was "extremely reassuring" after suffering a "sudden indisposition".
Sheikh Saad, born in 1930 and heir apparent, has been prime minister since 1978. He was educated in Kuwait and at Britain's Hendon Police Training School.
Six years after a U.S.-led military coalition freed Kuwait from Iraqi occupation, Sheikh Saad remains strongly opposed to direct contacts with Baghdad.
Kuwait, a founder of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, produces about two million barrels of oil per day and controls 10 percent of the world's proven oil reserves.
